h2: Start turtlesim
title: Start turtlesim

steps.does: T1 Starts the turtle program. A blue window opens with one turtle in the middle. Leave this running.

h2: Go back to the starting state
title: Go back to the starting state

steps.does: Clears the drawing and moves the turtle back to the middle.
Removes the second turtle called scout . Only needed if you already ran the spawn demo on slide 20.
Sets the red part of the background back to 69.
Sets the green part back to 86.
Sets the blue part back to 255. Together, 69 / 86 / 255 is turtlesim's normal blue.

h2: Three things that break the demo
title: Interaction Models

steps.does: T2 Sends a speed command 10 times per second. linear.x is forward speed. angular.z is turning speed. Forward and turning at the same time draws a circle.

h2: Three things that break the demo
title: Interaction Models

steps.does: T2 Asks one node to describe itself. It answers with everything it listens to, everything it sends, and everything it offers to others.
Lists the channels that exist right now.
Lists the services and their types. -t adds the type in square brackets. grep -v parameter hides the parameter services so the list stays short.
Lists the long jobs this node can be asked to do.
Lists the settings inside the node.

h2: Three things that break the demo
title: Interface Definitions

steps.does: T2 Prints the fields of the Twist message. Twist is the message every ROS 2 robot uses for speed commands.
Prints the same message as an empty example, ready to fill in. Copy it into the ros2 topic pub command from slide 6 and change one number.

h2: Three things that break the demo
title: Interface Definitions

steps.does: T2 Prints the message a laser scanner sends. This is the message you will use in Week 6 and Week 11.

h2: Three things that break the demo
title: Interface Definitions

steps.does: T2 Prints the small message that sits at the top of almost every sensor message.
T2 Prints the header of one real laser message. --once means one message then stop. --field header means print only that part. Gazebo must be running (T3) for this line.

h2: Three things that break the demo
title: Interface Definitions

steps.does: T2 Prints a service definition. srv in the name means service.
Prints an action definition. action in the name means action.

h2: Three things that break the demo
title: Topics

steps.does: T2 Prints every message the turtle sends about its own position. It never stops. Leave it running while you talk, then press Ctrl-C .

h2: Three things that break the demo
title: Topics

steps.does: T2 Prints one message and exits. Use this instead of Ctrl-C when you only need to see the structure.
Prints the message type of a channel, and how many nodes are connected to each end.
Starts sending again, in a second terminal, so you can compare the counts. Leave it running for the next line.
The same question again, while data is flowing. Then press Ctrl-C on the publisher and run it a third time — the count goes back to 0.

h2: Three things that break the demo
title: Services

steps.does: T2 Lists the services turtlesim offers, with their types.
Asks for the type of one service on its own. You need this type to call the service on slide 20.
The same list without the filter. Six more services appear, all with parameter in the name. Point at them and say: those are Part 6.

h2: Three things that break the demo
title: Services

steps.does: T2 Finds the name /spawn and its type turtlesim/srv/Spawn .

steps.cmd: ros2 service call /spawn turtlesim/srv/Spawn '{x: 2.0, y: 8.0, theta: 0.0, name: "scout"}'
steps.does: Asks turtlesim to add a second turtle. The three parts are: the name of the service, its type, and the request in curly brackets. x and y are the position, theta the heading.

h2: Three things that break the demo
title: Services

steps.does: T2 Removes the second turtle again.

h2: Three things that break the demo
title: Actions

steps.does: T2 Lists the actions and their types. turtlesim has exactly one.
Shows which nodes offer this action and which nodes are using it.

h2: Three things that break the demo
title: Actions

steps.does: T2 Prints the three parts of the action.

h2: Three things that break the demo
title: Actions

steps.does: T2 Asks the turtle to turn to heading 0.12 radians. --feedback means "show me the progress while it runs". Without that word you only see the final result.
The same job with no --feedback . You get the goal, then silence, then the result. The difference between these two runs is the whole reason actions exist.

h2: Three things that break the demo
title: Parameters

steps.does: T2 Lists every setting inside the running node.

h2: Three things that break the demo
title: Parameters

steps.does: T2 Shows what the node said when it declared this parameter — its type, its description, and its allowed range. Optional, but it makes the code slide concrete.

h2: Three things that break the demo
title: Parameters

steps.does: T2 Reads one setting out of the running node.
Changes the red channel to 200. Watch the T1 window as you press Enter.
Lowers the green channel to 60.
Lowers the blue channel to 60. The window is now red.

h2: Three things that break the demo
title: Application to a Mobile Robot

steps.does: T3 Tells the TurtleBot 3 packages which robot model to load. burger is the small one with a laser scanner.
Starts the simulator with a robot in a small world. A launch file starts many nodes at once. Wait 20 to 30 seconds.
T2 The same command as slide 7, on a different robot. The list is longer, but the command did not change.
Prints how far this laser can see, in metres.
Prints where the robot thinks it is. The dots mean "go inside this field, then inside that one".

h2: Three things that break the demo
title: Application to a Mobile Robot

steps.does: T2 Measures how many messages arrive per second. This is the command that answers "is data really arriving?". Press Ctrl-C after about 8 seconds.
Prints the delivery rules of the channel — the QoS , or quality of service. These are the promises the connection makes.

h2: Three things that break the demo
title: Custom Interface Packages

steps.does: T2 Counts the packages installed on this computer. wc -l counts lines.
Prints the folder where one package was installed.

deck: Deck B — Your Own Packages and Interfaces
h2: Three things that break the demo
title: Custom Interface Packages

steps.does: T2 Moves into the src folder of the workspace you made in Week 2. New packages always go here.
Creates the package that will hold your message and service definitions. It uses ament_cmake because turning a .msg file into a class you can import is a CMake job.

steps.cmd: ros2 pkg create ee414_w03_nodes --build-type ament_python --dependencies rclpy std_msgs
steps.does: Creates the package that will hold your Python nodes, the same way as last week. --dependencies writes the two names into package.xml for you.

deck: Deck B — Your Own Packages and Interfaces
h2: Three things that break the demo
title: Custom Interface Packages

steps.cmd: ros2 pkg create --build-type ament_python --dependencies rclpy std_msgs ee414_w03_nodes
steps.does: T2 Nothing. It fails. The only change from slide 5 is that the package name is now at the end .

deck: Deck B — Your Own Packages and Interfaces
h2: Three things that break the demo
title: Custom Interface Packages

steps.does: T2 Moves into the interfaces package you just created.
Creates the two folders. The names must be exactly msg and srv — the generator looks for those names.

deck: Deck B — Your Own Packages and Interfaces
h2: Three things that break the demo
title: Custom Interface Packages

steps.does: T2 Moves to the top of the workspace. Always build from here , never from inside a package.
Builds every package in the workspace. --symlink-install links your Python files instead of copying them, so small edits do not need a rebuild.
Tells this terminal where the new packages are. Without this line, the next command cannot find your message. Every new terminal needs it again.

deck: Deck B — Your Own Packages and Interfaces
h2: Three things that break the demo
title: Custom Interface Packages

steps.does: T2 Asks ROS 2 to print your message. The same command as slide 12 of Deck A, now pointed at something you wrote.
Prints your service. One separator, as expected.

h2: Three things that break the demo

steps.does: T2 Reads one message off the channel and prints it.

h2: Three things that break the demo
title: Service Server and Client

steps.does: T4 Starts the node that offers the /reset_odom service. Open a second tab for this — the wheel publisher must keep running.

deck: Deck B — Your Own Packages and Interfaces
h2: Three things that break the demo
title: Service Server and Client

steps.does: T2 Finds your service in the list. grep reset keeps only the lines containing that word.
Calls your service and waits for the reply. Same three parts as Deck A slide 20: name, type, request.

h2: Three things that break the demo
title: Executor Deadlock

steps.does: T2 Runs the client in the first wrong way. --ros-args -p name:=value is how you set a parameter when starting a node. This is meant to fail.

deck: Deck B — Your Own Packages and Interfaces
h2: Three things that break the demo
title: Executor Deadlock

steps.does: T2 Runs the client in the second wrong way. It prints two lines and then freezes forever. Press Ctrl-C when you are ready.

deck: Deck B — Your Own Packages and Interfaces
h2: Three things that break the demo
title: Executor Deadlock

steps.does: T2 Runs the same program the correct way. Press Ctrl-C when the class has seen it.

deck: Deck B — Your Own Packages and Interfaces
h2: Three things that break the demo
title: Parameters

steps.does: T4 Starts a node that prints its two settings every 2 seconds. Leave it running and keep it visible.

deck: Deck B — Your Own Packages and Interfaces
h2: Three things that break the demo
title: Parameters

steps.does: T2 Lists the settings of your own node, the same way as turtlesim's.
Reads the current speed limit.
Lowers the limit while the node runs. Watch T4.
Reads it back, to prove the change was kept.

deck: Deck B — Your Own Packages and Interfaces
h2: Three things that break the demo
title: Parameters

steps.does: Starts it again. The value you set is gone.
T2 Prints all current values as YAML. A fast way to save what you tuned before you type it into the launch file.

deck: Deck B — Your Own Packages and Interfaces
h2: Three things that break the demo
title: Action Clients

steps.does: T4 Starts a ready-made action server that computes Fibonacci numbers slowly, on purpose. Open a third tab . It comes with ROS 2; you do not have to write it.
T2 Asks for the first 3 numbers and shows the progress. Watch the sequence grow by one number per update.
The same goal with no --feedback . You wait in silence, then get the answer. The difference between these two runs is the entire reason actions exist.
